How it works

A dispatcher between you and a mechanic who knows your engine. Here is every step, and what you pay.

  1. 1

    You post or call

    Boat, engine make and model, hours if you know them, what it's doing, where it sits, and photos if you have them.

  2. 2

    A person calls you back

    Within 5 minutes during the day. We confirm the details and make sure it's a job we can help with.

  3. 3

    We offer it to the best-matched mechanics

    Two or three insured independents near you who work on your engine brand. The first to accept gets the job and texts you their name and a time window.

  4. 4

    You approve a written quote

    For anything beyond a diagnostic visit, the quote arrives by text or email and you accept it with one tap. Parts are billed at the final amount. If the job changes, the mechanic asks you first.

  5. 5

    The work happens at the boat

    You don't need to be there. The mechanic sends photos of the work and the old parts.

  6. 6

    You pay when it's done

    A link shows the itemized invoice. Pay by bank transfer at the invoiced amount, or by card with a small processing fee shown up front. We pay the mechanic.

How mechanics are checked

  • Years of experience and brand certifications
  • Commercial general liability insurance, with the certificate on file and renewals tracked
  • A signed standards agreement: show up, quote in writing, honor the quote, clean up
  • Customer reviews on every job, visible to our dispatchers

What it costs

You pay the mechanic's price. Mobile marine labor in Tampa Bay runs about $120 to $150 an hour, with a trip or diagnostic fee around $75 to $150 that is usually credited toward the repair. Our fee comes out of the mechanic's side, in exchange for sending them work and handling the billing.
